title: Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: Symptom-cause-fix tables per subsystem prevent recurring bugs (e.g. DNS-desync scar, save-tier corruption); knowledge-gap detection when MCP retrieval returns zero results (case study 3, drop-system) surfaces undocumented subsystems before risky refactors.
cita: Vasilopoulos, A. (2026). Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase.
notes: Systems/experience-report, no controlled ablation -> CUALITATIVA (Sec 4.1). Sec 3 tiered arch: T1 constitution ~660L hot-load / T2 19 specialist agents ~9300L / T3 34 KB docs ~16250L, MCP retrieval uses keyword substring matching (Sec 3.3.1) -> retrieval=GREP-ARCHIVOS. Sec 4.2-4.3 quant: 283 sessions, 2801 human prompts, 16522 agent turns, 1478 MCP calls/218 sessions (usage counts, not precision -> mide_lectura=NO). 4 case studies Sec 4.4 (save-system 74 sessions zero bugs; UI-sync pattern reuse; drop-system knowledge-gap-as-signal; RNG determinism collaborative debugging). multiagente=SI: 19 domain-expert agents share T1/T3 knowledge via orchestration trigger table. trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM: specs 'generated and updated by the AI at the developer's direction', no deterministic write rule defined.

title: Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems
benchmarks: Superstore Sales; UCI Adult Income; NYC 311 Service Requests; World Bank GDP
fallos_mitigaciones: Full-history persistence causes 'trace anchoring': agent biased toward stale prior solution paths, degrading completion 8pp below no-memory baseline (Sec 6.2/7, Table 1-2); mitigated by selective forgetting (Sec 3.3): discard reasoning traces, tool-invocation logs, error-recovery paths, raw data; keep only 4 structured memory categories.
cita: Pedada, S., Dhavala, A., & Patil, N. (2026). Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems.
notes: Sec 3.2 decomposes memory into Mtask/Mdata/Mtools/Moutput, persisted to MongoDB + git-versioned artifacts (Eq.1-3) -> representacion=HIBRIDA. Sec 3.3 explicit 'selective forgetting' (deterministic app-layer filtering at session end, not LLM judgment) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA; retrieval=NA (no ranking/search step, all 4 categories composed wholesale into next prompt, Eq.1-2). Table 1 ablation (no-mem 79% / full-hist 71% / selective 96% completion, 24 enterprise tasks); Table 2 public-dataset replication (12/12 zero-token refresh trials); Table 3 summary-driven token reduction 97-946x -> F add COSTO. Sec 3.5 zero-token refresh checks schema-compatibility before reuse (staleness/fidelity gate) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. F facet MULTIAGENTE kept from screening (workspace 'shared...collaborative' across users, Sec 1.1 UC2) though strict RQ4 multiagente=NO (collaboration is human-user sharing via RBAC, not multiple AI agents; single agentic engine per session, Sec 5). Moutput = runtime-injection 'contract' between artifact and data -> handoff includes CONTRATO. Use cases include explicit cross-team org sharing (Sec 1.1 UC2) -> alcance adds ORGANIZACION.

title: Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks
benchmarks: SWE-bench
fallos_mitigaciones: Hallucination detection (AST-based validation flagging non-existent APIs, incorrect signatures, phantom dependencies) tracked as a metric (Sec 2.3, 'Comprehensive Metrics Collection'); no explicit mitigation strategy is described beyond flagging results.
cita: Murugesan, T. (2026). Enhancing SWE Bench with Context Engineering: A Comparative Study Against Prompt Engineering in LLM-Based Software Tasks.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: paper reads as likely synthetic/low-substance (single-author, generic citations to unnamed venues [1]-[4] for all quantitative claims, illustrative Python code blocks in Sec 2.3 contain syntax gaps typical of AI-generated pseudocode) -- decision left to human per protocol. mem_tipos=NA per rule 5: paper is NOT about persistent cross-session memory, it measures single-task 'context engineering' (repo history/docs/architecture injected per SWE-bench task, discarded after) vs prompt engineering on SWE-bench success (Sec 2.3 Methodology, 240 stratified tasks, 3 conditions: baseline/prompt-eng/context-eng). retrieval=RANKING: 3-stage pipeline (traversal, relevance scoring, structuring) explicitly scores/prioritizes context (Sec 2.2). mide_lectura=SI: hybrid scoring reports '78% alignment with expert developer judgments of context relevance' (Sec 2.3) -> F requires+gets RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (differs from F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO only). Sec 2.4: context-eng +29.3% avg success on complex multi-component tasks vs +4.2% for prompt-eng alone; prompt-eng +14% on simple single-file tasks. F also adds COSTO (extensive token/resource-consumption metrics, Sec 2.3).

title: .ava: A Compressed Symbolic Notation for Persistent AI Agent Memory
benchmarks: NINGUNO
fallos_mitigaciones: V3 dataset design (overweighted key symbols x15, 5 epochs) caused severe overfitting, worse than V2 on nearly all metrics (Sec 4.3.3, 'echec'); mitigated in V4/V4b by switching to prompt/completion loss (SFTTrainer), zero duplication with paraphrase diversity, and tuning to 3 epochs (Sec 4.3.4-4.3.5).
cita: Cros, A. & Ava (2026). .ava -- Une notation symbolique compressee pour la memoire persistante d'agents IA.
notes: Sec 2.5 Table 2: measured compression on real MEMORY.md (~24K char -> ~800 char, ~30x, full file 661 lines). Sec 4.3.5 V4b fine-tune result: loss 0.999, token accuracy 78.5% (vs 51% for V4 1-epoch) on Qwen2.5-1.5B/6GB VRAM LoRA -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION (V1-V4b dataset/training iterations, Table with loss/accuracy per phase) + MEDICION-COSTO (compression ratios Table 2, GPU/time Sec 4.3.5). Sec 3.5: 4-layer memory hierarchy L1 active-context / L2 hot .ava (WRITE) / L3 warm semantic-search via Ollama+nomic-embed-text (retrieval=EMBEDDINGS) / L4 cold full archive never deleted (explicit anti-OLVIDO design principle, Sec 3.4: 'IA doit garder tout'). Sec 2.3 vocabulary includes project-state symbols (triangle=project name/stack/metrics, with terminal state active/paused/off/dead/merged) -> plan_estado=SI (project/progress state IS memory content). F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO confirmed (.ava files are git-versionable plain text, Sec 2.2 principle 4); F adds COSTO since compression/token-economy is the paper's central contribution.

title: SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution
benchmarks: SWE-Bench Lite; SWE-Bench Pro
fallos_mitigaciones: Failed-hypothesis reversion via checkpoint rollback: agent reverts to prior semantic-step checkpoint when later edits fail, then branches a new hypothesis (Sec 3.3, Fig 2 a-2); Table 4 ablation shows resolve-rate drop when substituting SWE-Adept's designed planning/checkpointing module with SWE-agent's free-form think-and-edit loop.
cita: He, K., & Roy, K. (2026). SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution.
notes: Sec 3.1 code-structure tree (tree-sitter, dependency graph) drives agent-directed depth-first search (Fig 1) -> retrieval=GRAFO; Table 1 reports Acc@3(file)/Acc@5(function) localization accuracy -> mide_lectura=SI, requires+has RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F (confirms F_screening). Sec 3.3 'backend working memory' (TRABAJO) stores hypothesis/todo/checkpoint metadata (git hash) keyed by semantic execution step -> representacion=HIBRIDA (structured metadata + git); trigger=CHECKPOINT (agent commits state 'after each completed to-do step', literal vocab match). Sec 3.3/Fig 2c: 'compile a comparative report across hypotheses... to support final selection' -> operaciones includes CONSOLIDACION. Table 2 resolve rate +2.8-4.3pp vs baselines on SWE-Bench Lite/Pro with GPT-5.2/Claude-4.5; Table 4-5 module + context-management ablations. hypothesis_plan todo lists w/ status [-]/[v]/[!] tracked in memory -> plan_estado=SI. handoff=PUNTEROS: resolution agent receives identified code locations (file+line 'anchors') from localization agent, not full content (Sec 3.3). Two-agent framework (localization+resolution) with separate context windows -> multiagente=SI, added to F (differs from F_screening which lacked MULTIAGENTE).

title: DocAware: Documentation-Augmented AI Agents for Reliable Code Review and API Migration
benchmarks: openai-v3; express-v4; stripe-v2; mongoose-v6; axios-v0 (self-constructed fixtures, Sec 4.2)
fallos_mitigaciones: Hallucination (findings referencing API names absent from retrieved docs) measured at 22.9-25.7% even WITH documentation (Sec 5.3, Table 2); mitigated but not eliminated via structured/version-specific doc retrieval + tool-use structured output; authors flag the metric only checks syntactic grounding, not semantic correctness (Sec 5.3/6.2).
cita: Chandrashekar, P. (2026). DocAware: Documentation-Augmented AI Agents for Reliable Code Review and API Migration.
notes: Sec 3.4 persistent memory layer: entry types review_finding/migration_decision/pattern/annotation, vector embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, 384-dim) + cosine-similarity JSON index -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Sec 5.1 Table 2: 4-condition A/B/C/D ablation (F1 70.9%->86.8%, recall 76.4%->98.6%; D vs C isolates memory's contribution: +0.3 F1pp/+0.4 precisionpp) -> mide_lectura=SI (memory-read utility explicitly measured), F confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO from F_screening. Sec 5.3: hallucination-rate is a central measured outcome across doc conditions -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (paper's core claim is grounding/fidelity against version-specific docs). Sec 4.2: 5 self-built JS-library migration fixtures, 31 real issues + 6 decoys, not an established external benchmark. handoff=CONTENIDO: review findings/patterns/decisions persist and are retrieved in later review sessions of the same project (Sec 3.4, RQ4.Q3).

title: The Markdown Fallacy: Empirical Evidence That Format Is the Wrong Debate for LLM Memory Architecture
benchmarks: Custom 50-document/50-query Google-Ads-MCC benchmark (this paper, open-sourced); data.world KG benchmark and GraphRAG-Bench cited as external comparison points (Sec II-C)
fallos_mitigaciones: GraphRAG scored notably lower on Level-2 relational queries (0.731) because the extracted subgraph captured entities/relationships but lost the explanatory narrative/mechanism prose (Sec IV.D 'GraphRAG Level 2 Anomaly'); proposed direction is preserving explanatory metadata alongside structural relationships, not yet implemented.
cita: Williams, J. (2026). The Markdown Fallacy: Empirical Evidence That Format Is the Wrong Debate for LLM Memory Architecture.
notes: mem_tipos=NA per rule 5: this is a controlled measurement/benchmark study of FORMAT and RETRIEVAL-ARCHITECTURE effects on LLM reasoning accuracy, not a proposal of a persistent memory mechanism (Sec III Methodology, H1-H3). Stage 1 (Sec IV.A, N=900, Table I): markdown vs structured-relational encoding, format has no consistent directional effect (delta=-0.004 overall). Stage 2 (Sec IV.B, N=1200, Table II): full-context markdown (0.964) significantly beats Vector-RAG (0.888), GraphRAG (0.875) and Hybrid (0.904) on L3 strategic queries (ANOVA p<0.004) -> mide_lectura=SI (retrieval quality is THE measured variable), F confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (matches F_screening). Table III: retrieval conditions retain only 10.6-16.2% of the 33,122-char corpus (84-90% information loss) -- reframes the debate as an information-budget/COSTO problem at production scale (Sec V.D 'Scale Threshold'), hence F adds COSTO.

title: Temporal-Stratified Retrieval for AI Agent Memory: A Structure-First Alternative to Vector Search
benchmarks: 500-atom / 100-query synthetic benchmark (self-constructed, reproducible via benchmarks/run_benchmark.py, Sec 4.1)
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec 5.2 Limitations: cannot match semantically-related-but-lexically-different queries without embeddings (e.g. 'revenue' vs 'sales'), only partially mitigated by explicit tagging; linear-scan manifest scoring degrades above ~10,000 atoms (no inverted index yet); scoring weights are hand-tuned/unvalidated on diverse domains.
cita: Hartmann, A. (2026). Temporal-Stratified Retrieval for AI Agent Memory: A Structure-First Alternative to Vector Search.
notes: Sec 3.1 atom schema: YAML frontmatter, 9 required fields, 14 types spanning episodic (incident/event/lesson/loss/win) and semantic (rule/insight/reference/concept) knowledge -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA;SEMANTICA. Sec 3.3 hot(<=2d)/warm(2-7d)/cold(>7d) temporal stratification by 'updated' field -> operaciones+CONSOLIDACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (time-threshold based, not LLM judgment). Sec 3.4 deterministic weighted keyword scoring (name/tag/project/description/path) + multi-keyword bonus + temporal bonus + archived(x0.3)/superseded(x0.5) status PENALTY -- the status penalty is an explicit staleness-aware scoring adjustment -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI; scoring=RANKING (not plain grep, it's a multi-factor weighted algorithm). Sec 4.1 benchmark (500 atoms/100 queries): mean latency 1.62ms, 100/100 top-1 precision on tag-matched queries, hot layer top-1 in 66% of cases -> mide_lectura=SI confirms RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (matches F_screening). Sec 4.2 production deployment (470 atoms/14 projects) explicitly labelled 'observational findings (not controlled measurements)' -> evidencia_tipo adds CUALITATIVA alongside the controlled BENCHMARK-E2E.

title: Beyond RAG: LLM Wikis as Living Semantic Memory: Patterns, Empirical Findings, and Open Problems
benchmarks: Self-constructed studies, no named external benchmark: CLS-Wiki consolidation-gating study (AUC), cross-institutional policy-retrieval citation-recall study, confidence-calibration (ECE) study, KTRR six-layer routing study on a 2,718-unit NingboTech AI-course corpus (111 files, academic years 2021-2026, Sec 3.1)
fallos_mitigaciones: Abstract/Sec4.2: 'the wiki pattern failed to outperform RAG in two tested domains' (explicit negative result). Sec 2.5: three degenerate-compiler failure modes (fragmentation, atomisation, over-merging) plus an 'LLM filter saturation' regime -- an ingest-value pre-filter becomes uninformative (assigns high value to nearly every document) when the wiki is small relative to the incoming document stream, characteristic of the early flywheel phase; no full fix proposed, flagged as a deployment risk.
cita: Zhang, B. (2026). Beyond RAG: LLM Wikis as Living Semantic Memory: Patterns, Empirical Findings, and Open Problems.
notes: Self-described 'position paper... not a system description' synthesising first-person empirical sub-studies -> evidencia_tipo mixes ABLATION/MEDICION-COSTO/CUALITATIVA. Sec 2.4: wiki-based retrieval citation recall 0.242+-0.21 vs BM25-RAG 0.095+-0.12 (2.5x) on cross-institutional policy queries -> mide_lectura=SI, F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Sec 2.2 CLS-Wiki study: outcome-surprise AUC=0.720 predicting episodic-to-semantic consolidation value. Sec 2.3: raw LLM-confidence-label Expected Calibration Error 0.528, reduced to 0.311 by post-hoc propagation framework. Sec 3.1 six-layer KTRR knowledge lattice (Raw/Wiki/Protocol/Metadata/Fact/Rule) with cost-sensitive LLM-judged ingest-routing classifier -> operaciones+ADMISION. Sec3.2-3.3 lint/contradiction-detection + staleness/drift + Sec3.4 provenance/audit-trails -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (central contribution). 'Failed to outperform RAG in two tested domains' -> F NEGATIVO sense(b): evidence AGAINST the memory approach (per rule7), matches F_screening. Sec 7.2 distributed/multi-agent wikis explicitly named an OPEN problem, not implemented -> multiagente=NO.

title: CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories
benchmarks: 5 public repos (self-constructed illustrative case study, Sec V.B): psf/requests, pallets/flask, expressjs/express, redis/redis, junit-team/junit5 (25,000 commits); git log --grep and BM25 used as comparison baselines, not named external benchmarks
fallos_mitigaciones: RQ5 (n=200, two LLM judges): no retrieval condition (CommitDistill, BM25, or CD-Hybrid) produces a statistically detectable lift over a no-retrieval control on the headline mean, and CD-Hybrid is indistinguishable from BM25 head-to-head -- an explicit negative downstream-utility finding, honestly reported rather than hidden (Sec I / VI-G2). Mitigation for over-confident retrieval: calibrated silence threshold theta=2.5 gives a 'helps or stays silent' abstention property on out-of-corpus/OOD queries (Sec VI-E).
cita: Chukkapalli, D., Avula, T., Aggarwal, A., Singh, H., & Tallanki, A. (2026). CommitDistill: A Lightweight Knowledge-Centric Memory Layer for Software Repositories.
notes: Abstract: 1,167 typed units (Facts/Skills/Patterns) from 25,000 commits, useful-precision 0.525 @ Cohen's kappa=0.633 (40 dual-annotated Python units, RQ2) -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(Facts);PROCEDIMENTAL(Skills);EPISODICA(Patterns, recurring past-failure records). Sec VI.D 'decisive empirical finding': budget-constrained hit-rate at 256-char/query CommitDistill 0.750 vs BM25 0.333 vs git-log-grep 0.083 -> mide_lectura=SI (F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, matches F_screening). Sec III.D: extraction triggers as a post-merge/post-issue git hook -> EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Sec II.C.3/IV.D: every unit carries commit-SHA/author/date provenance, stored as plain diffable JSON, reviewable via git diff -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI ('trust-instrumented memory substrate'). RQ5 top-3 typed units prepended to an LLM coding assistant's context at decision time (Sec V.A) -> handoff=CONTENIDO. Authors explicitly frame the evaluation as an 'illustrative case study... not for hypothesis testing' (Sec V.A) and report the null RQ5 result forthrightly -> F NEGATIVO sense(b), matches F_screening.

title: Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents
benchmarks: ALFWorld; SkillsBench
fallos_mitigaciones: Motivating failure mode (Sec 1): a 'confused -> re-retrieve -> still confused' loop where prose skill docs force the agent to re-derive schema+invocation syntax on every retrieval, producing off-by-one action errors ('put X in/on Y' vs 'move X to Y'); mitigated by the typed-contract + concrete-action-template dual signal (Sec 3.5, Fig 2). 2/10 SkillsBench SaP runs still crashed mid-execution (court-form-filling, data-to-d3) despite token savings (Sec 5.3).
cita: Li, X., Zang, Y., Cao, Y., & Sun, A. (2026). Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents.
notes: Sec3.3 four-check deterministic verifier (Coverage, Binding, Replacement, Risk) gates which candidate clusters get promoted into typed contracts kappa (trigger/input_schema/output_schema/pre-postconditions) -> operaciones ADMISION; Coverage+Replacement checks explicitly verify the compiled contract stays faithful to / coherently substitutes the source prose -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Table1: ALFWorld 134-game pooled 3 seeds (n=402): SaP wins 82 vs GoS 47 (+74% relative, pooled McNemar p=8.2e-5) at -22.8+-6.4% input tok / -17.3+-5.1% output tok / -14.5+-4.1% LLM calls per game -> mide_lectura=SI (the paper's central claim IS that the retrieved-content REPRESENTATION improves downstream task success), F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (differs from F_screening, noted here). Table3: pipeline ablation (deterministic-only -> +RC -> +BE) each stage adds ~5pp reward, ALFWorld 20-game pilot. Table2: SkillsBench 10-task (gpt-5-codex): SaP 3/10 vs GoS 2/10 at -43% input tokens. Sec3.1: cross-parent factoring promotes contracts callable in multiple parent skills to shared child skills -> operaciones CONSOLIDACION. Retrieval-time 'substituted bundle' (Fig2) delivers concrete action templates + rewritten parent skeleton + inlined typed contract -> handoff=CONTENIDO;CONTRATO (kappa literally named a 'contract' with trigger/I-O schema/pre-post-conditions).

title: Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory
benchmarks: 10-case SRS dataset (self-constructed, Table 2); baseline comparison against MetaGPT (not a named external benchmark)
fallos_mitigaciones: RQ2 (Sec 5.2/Table 4): RAG-based knowledge infusion improves component coupling/abstraction and mitigates 'God Object' anti-patterns seen in the noRAG condition, but REDUCES cohesion and increases interface/behavioral-state complexity inconsistently across the 10 projects -- 'does not consistently improve all quality metrics', a mixed/negative finding about the memory-infusion mechanism reported forthrightly.
cita: Li, R., Zhang, Y., Zhou, X., Cai, Y., Liang, P., Sun, W., Xuan, J., Jin, Z., & Liu, Y. (2026). Bridging Requirements and Architecture: Multi-Agent Orchestration with External Knowledge and Hierarchical Memory.
notes: Sec3.1/3.3, Fig1: explicit 3-tier hierarchical memory (per-agent working memory + per-agent episodic memory recording design experiences + framework-level SHARED semantic memory distilled from software projects/literature/expert knowledge, citing cognitive-architecture ref [49]) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO;EPISODICA;SEMANTICA (literal vocab match). 4 specialized agents (Analyst/Modeler/Designer/Evaluator) ALL access the shared semantic memory (Sec3.1: 'all agents can access and retrieve') -> multiagente=SI, added to F (differs materially from F_screening=DOCS-VERSIONADO only, flagged). RQ2/Table4: RAG(with) vs noRAG structural+quantitative ablation across 10 SRS cases isolates the knowledge-infusion effect -> mide_lectura=SI, F+RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (also differs from screening). Evaluator agent produces an ATAM evaluation report + a 'mismatch analysis report' explicitly checking consistency between generated artifacts and requirements at every pipeline stage -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, F+FIDELIDAD. Shared semantic memory 'distills' knowledge from prior sources -> operaciones+CONSOLIDACION. F_screening's DOCS-VERSIONADO is a comparatively WEAK fit (paper's 'documentation' = produced architecture-doc OUTPUT artifact, not a git-versioned memory-file substrate like the other papers in this batch); kept for the reviewer's spot-check per rule4.

title: Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline
benchmarks: LoCoMo, HotpotQA, AMABench-ALF, AMABench-Web, AMABench-T2SQL, MemoryAgentBench (AR/TTL/LRU/CR), ALFWorld, MemoryArena-shop, MemoryArena-travel
fallos_mitigaciones: Representation-level failure (HippoRAG's entity-relation KG drops step/action indices, Fig.2) mitigated by widening schema at build time. Retrieval-level failure (PlugMem's passive router returns compact note, raw trace stays unread, Table 4) mitigated by active agent-driven retrieval (follow-up calls, AutoMEM). Gap2 (S4.5): text procedural rules cannot encode state-dependent decisions (17/32 ALFWorld failures persist w/ golden memory); no mitigation short of parametric RL update.
cita: Chen et al. (2026). Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline.
notes: S4.2 Fig.2/Table4: representation-level failure (HippoRAG entity-KG drops step/action labels) vs retrieval-level failure (PlugMem keeps ~98% info in episodic store but passive router fails, Table 4 oracle 98% overall). AutoMEM (S5, Algorithm 1) = agentic harness w/ rg/read/dump/index_query menu over flat-text + Cypher graph index; +22.3pp over DCI-Lite and +5.8pp over long-context on LoCoMo (67.3 vs 61.5), best avg rank 3.10. Fig.1/Fig.3 track token+latency cost, amortization crossover N~=2(LightMem)/N~=32(HippoRAG) vs DCI-Lite. S4.5 Table7: golden procedural memory on ALFWorld raises SR 43.3%->71.7% (GRPO post-train 86.7%), motivating PROCEDIMENTAL. F differs from F_screening (DOCS-VERSIONADO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO): added COSTO (extensive amortization/latency analysis) + PROCEDIMENTAL (golden procedural memory ablation, S4.5).

title: Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory
benchmarks: MemoryAgentBench (AR/TTL/LRU/SF: SH-QA, MH-QA, LongMemEval S*, EventQA, MCC, Rec@5, Summ, DetQA, FactConsolidation SH/MH)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory fragmentation, memory conflict, long-history compression loss, retrieval-insufficient-for-reasoning (Fig.1, 4 challenges) mitigated by topic-structured documents + buffered CURRENT->split/merge consolidation + agentic iterative retrieval. Multi-hop selective forgetting (FC-MH) remains a structural limit: single-hop settled at write time via recency override, but no single rewrite pass enforces cross-document consistency for multi-hop chains (81.0% FC-SH vs 35.0% FC-MH, S4.2).
cita: Ji et al. (2026). Infini Memory: Maintainable Topic Documents for Long-Term LLM Agent Memory.
notes: S3.2-3.3 topic documents (doc_id/summary/metadata + entry seq/time/source tags) w/ buffered CURRENT->split/merge consolidation (Eq.1 flush=|C|>=5000tok OR delta_t threshold, S4.1). S3.4 agentic retrieval (grep/grep_doc/search/list_docs/read_lines, up to 7 rounds) + BM25 fallback = GREP-ARCHIVOS;RANKING. Table1: Infini Memory-A 64.7% overall on MemoryAgentBench, +19.2pp over best baseline (REMem 46.6/HippoRAG-v2 45.5), best on all 4 axes (AR+12.5,TTL+4.4,LRU+25.4,SF+26.5). Table2/Fig6-7 ablations: removing structural maint. -6.7 to -10.0pp (76.0->69.3%); single-shot summary-only retrieval -37.6pp vs hybrid. F differs from F_screening (DOCS-VERSIONADO;CONSOLIDACION): added FIDELIDAD (seq/time/source provenance tags enable supersede/staleness resolution, S3.2) + RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (mide_lectura=SI, Table2 retrieval ablation).

title: Assessing Continuity in Agentic Development Across Multiple Development Cycles
benchmarks: Mock LLM-dashboard web project (custom benchmark, no external SMS benchmark); Codex CLI agent, Bosch R&D Center Lund multi-agent factory pipeline
fallos_mitigaciones: Difficulty in decision adherence (decision1 'append text to headings' only 33.33% success in comb 3&4 vs decision2 'add timestamp' 11.11-61.11%) attributed to training-data bias and prompt wording (S5.1.1); no strategy fully mitigates this. Time/token usage variation confounded by external factors (server load, network latency via VPN), not isolated experimentally (S5.1.2).
cita: Jonsater & Svensson (2026). Assessing Continuity in Agentic Development Across Multiple Development Cycles.
notes: S3.3.1: 3 strategies (to-do list JSON in agent-context/todo/, decision log in agent-context/decisions/, session summary) x 5 combinations (baseline/each alone/all three) x 3 iterations x 2 dev cycles, injected via AGENTS.md (Codex CLI), all context stored as JSON files in a context-folder ('context bank'). S5.1.1: decision1 success only 33.33% (comb 3&4), decision2 varies 11.11-61.11% across combos - no single strategy dominates all decisions; abstract reports combination 2 (decision log) best overall for decision consistency + cost/time efficiency. S1.6 explicit non-scope: 'does not address context sharing between multiple agents' -> multiagente=NO. F differs from F_screening (DOCS-VERSIONADO;WRITE): added PROCEDIMENTAL (to-do-list=explicit task-plan persistence, plan_estado=SI, S3.3 strategy 1) + COSTO (Fig.4.7/4.8 generation cost & temporal efficiency tracked as KPI). mide_lectura=NO: metrics measure end-to-end decision/requirement compliance, not isolated retrieval precision.

title: GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge
benchmarks: GPQA-Diamond, MATH-500, ScienceWorld
fallos_mitigaciones: H-memory (cross-problem memory improves accuracy) is REJECTED on novel problems across 5 substrates (none/markdown/vector/graph/git), 2 benchmarks, 2 backbones, n up to 500 (S4); a promising +15pp git trend at n=40 did NOT survive its own pre-registered replication at n=98 (+1.0pp) -- authors explicitly retract it (NEGATIVO sense b, evidencia negativa). cita: Shekar et al. (2026). GitOfThoughts: Version-Controlled Reasoning and Agent Memory You Can Replay, Diff, and Merge.

notes: S1 Memory Contamination Problem: (i) Attack Persistence - Table1 injection round1 (traj-len-4) 60.53% ASR vs round2 15.38%/round3 5.88%, due to full-accumulation ck=ck-1(+)tau_k (S2.1 formalization); (ii) Utility Degradation - Fig.4a utility 44.46%(short)->19.08%(long), 57% decline. title: Trojan Hippo: Weaponizing Agent Memory for Data Exfiltration

title: State Contamination in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents

fallos_mitigaciones: Memory laundering: toxic context compressed into memory summaries that fall below standard toxicity-classifier thresholds (tox(Mt)<tau) yet still causally increase downstream toxicity (SPG). Mitigation depends on placement: sanitizing toxic state BEFORE summarization (transcript control + memory control + DPO, 'full system') substantially reduces the hidden propagation gap (Table3: SPG 0.0149->0.0014, turn-final-tox 0.1207->0.0106), whereas cleaning only the completed summary (memory-only rewrite/gate) leaves laundered influence largely intact.

notes: S3.2-3.3 'state' = raw transcript + compressed running memory summary + retrieved context, scoped to the live multi-agent conversation (not persisted across sessions/projects) -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO, alcance=SESION. Memory update Mt=Summarize(Mt-1,xvt-1) applied every turn (deterministic, not an LLM-discretionary decision to write) -> trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA; this summarization step IS memory CONSOLIDACION and is the central mechanism of the failure mode (S5.2: 'Laundering originates at compression, not at post-hoc sanitization'). S4.2 write-gate W (stores generated message as-is/redacted/rewritten before it enters transcript/memory) -> ADMISION. Plain-text transcript/summary buffer, no vector/graph index -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS; the full running summary is always included in context rather than searched/ranked from a larger store -> retrieval=NA. title: Memory Contagion: Cross-Temporal Propagation of Evaluator Bias via Agent Memory

fallos_mitigaciones: Memory Contagion: evaluator bias in a source agent's experiences propagates cross-temporally to a target agent retrieving from the SAME memory store, even under perfect (oracle) consolidation (GammaA=13.18 length bias, p<0.01). Mitigation tested (LLM-based content-rewriting debiasing) is INCOMPLETE: efficacy ratio E4=0.90 (length) / 0.51 (authority), nonzero residual Gamma_debiased=0.70/4.20. Paper lists only future-work mitigations (statistical bias-detection tests, diversity-aware retrieval, periodic memory auditing, 'memory quarantine'), none validated here.
cita: Liu (2026). Memory Contagion: Cross-Temporal Propagation of Evaluator Bias via Agent Memory.

Consolidation triggered 'when new trajectories arrive' (oracle vs LLM-summarization merge compared, Table1) -> operaciones=WRITE;CONSOLIDACION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. Table3/S4.3 mechanism decomposition (E1 content=3.45, E2 retrieval=2.91, E3 interaction~0.5): BOTH content and retrieval pathways contribute, content slightly dominant -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. E4 debiasing sanity check is incomplete (see fallos_mitigaciones). Core contribution is NEGATIVE evidence: perfect/oracle consolidation does NOT prevent bias propagation, contradicting the assumption that fixing consolidation quality alone fixes memory-degradation problems (contra Zhang et al. 2026 cited in S1/S5) -> NEGATIVO(b) per rule7. No provenance/staleness/source-verification mechanism proposed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
benchmarks: MEM-INV-Bench (own; 12 domains x 5 consequential tool types, cross-defense x cross-attack x cross-model over 8 frontier models across 6 vendors)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory poisoning via 3 laundering channels: self-summarization (L-a), trusted-tool echo (L-b), manufactured corroboration (L-c) each erase an item's untrusted origin through a behavior-preserving transformation, defeating content- and lineage-based defenses (up to 68% laundering ASR). Mitigated via TMA-NM: non-malleable origin-bound authority (write-time binding M1 + non-malleable propagation M2 closing L-a/L-b) + Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation (M3, >=2 independent trusted principals, closing L-c) + tamper-evident verdict log (M4). Table1: TMA-NM reaches 0% ASR on direct attack AND laundering at 100% legit-utility (vs baselines: trust_score/capability_ifc 68% laundered, capability_ifc additionally 84% direct-ASR, lineage 47% laundered).

SIII M1 write-time origin binding = WRITE; M3 Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated ELEVATION raises an existing item's authority label via >=2 independent trusted principals or fresh user-auth -> ACTUALIZACION. M4 append-only tamper-evident hash-chain verdict log -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (structured tuple store + log, no vector/graph index specified); the retrieval mechanism itself is left unspecified/agnostic in the pipeline write->retrieve->act -> retrieval=NA. SIV formal TLA+ model + machine-checked theorems T1(malleable-gate insufficiency)/T2(write-time-binding necessity)/T3(non-malleable-authority sufficiency, 3270 reachable states) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (this IS the paper's core contribution: origin/provenance-bound authority). SII explicitly excludes 'cross-agent shared memory' as OUT OF SCOPE ('is out of scope and is the province of agent-communication-protocol security') -> multiagente=NO. SV MEM-INV-Bench: 12 domains x 5 consequential tool types x 5 defense classes (none/trust_score/lineage/capability_ifc/TMA-NM) x 8 frontier models (6 vendors) x {direct,L-a,L-b,L-c} + legit-utility/uncorr-auto controls. Table1 pooled results confirm baselines fail exactly where the separation theorem predicts -> evidencia_tipo=BENCHMARK-E2E, mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (legit-utility=100% control rules out block-everything tautology, directly measuring preserved read/act utility). Deployability: TMA-NM act-gate = 1.3us/decision vs ~2000ms for a content-detection judge call (~6 orders of magnitude cheaper); 'all runs report cost' -> COSTO/MEDICION-COSTO. Cross-model trigger-style study + 'the ablation isolates each mechanism' (SVI) -> evidencia_tipo also ABLATION. All TMA-NM-vs-baseline gaps significant at p<5e-5 (20,000-iteration permutation test). alcance: threat model explicitly 'store untrusted content in one session that later steers... in a future session' / 'weeks later, in an unrelated session' -> PROYECTO (persists across many sessions). title: Forensic Trajectory Signatures for Agent Memory Poisoning Detection
benchmarks: own P1 factorial dataset from prior work (Leong 2026): 2,520 labeled DTA runs (9 open-source models x 7 defense conditions x 40 runs); frontier probes GPT-4.1 (N=20 pre-populated + 405/560 expanded evaluation)
fallos_mitigaciones: Memory-channel poisoning (delayed-trigger attack, DTA): a malicious routing rule is stored in persistent memory in an early session and retrieved+executed (email exfiltration) in a later trigger session. Mitigation is a forensic TRAJECTORY DETECTOR (tool-call logs only, no memory-content access) exploiting the mechanistically-forced recall_before_send invariant: Recall=0.984-1.000/AUC=0.990 under 6/7 defense conditions; the ONE structural blind spot is the Memory-Sandbox condition (recall_fact tool removed), where an implicit-bypass attack variant (qwq:32b, goal-directed RAG fallback) evades detection entirely (all 31 FN). Evasion boundary: prompt-inline attacks (no memory write) score near the decision boundary (mean 0.541, Recall=0.35 only), explicitly enabling attack-vector attribution rather than full mitigation.
cita: Leong (2026). Forensic Trajectory Signatures for Agent Memory Poisoning Detection.
notes: S2.1-2.2 threat model: attacker injects a routing-rule key-value fact via RAG into persistent memory (memory.save_fact/recall_fact/list_all_facts tool API); exfiltration in a LATER trigger session S4 requires memory.recall_fact(key) before email.send_email -> underlying memory operations = WRITE(save_fact) + GREP-ARCHIVOS retrieval (exact key lookup by name, not ranked/embedding search); representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (key-value fact store). mem_tipos=NA: the paper's OWN contribution is a forensic TRAJECTORY classifier over tool-call logs (never memory contents/weights/activations/user messages, S2.1 'Detection constraint'), not a memory-content taxonomy. S2.2 dataset: 2,520 labeled DTA runs from prior work's P1 factorial (9 open-source models x 7 defense conditions x 40 runs; 1,919 attack-success/601 non-exfiltration). Table1: 19-feature Random Forest AUC=0.9904 (BCa 95%CI[0.987,0.993], N=10000 resamples), Recall=0.9838; single-rule baseline (recall_before_send alone) already AUC=0.9563 -> mechanistically forced by the attack's information-retrieval dependency (S3.3). Table6 feature-group ablation: removing ALL 9 recall-related features (half the feature set) leaves AUC UNCHANGED at 0.9904 -> overdetermined signature across independent channels -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION. Table4 cross-model hold-out (9 models, 7B-120B): AUC=1.000 on 6/9 models; 3 mechanistically-explained exceptions (qwq:32b implicit RAG-fallback bypass; qwen2.5:14b distributional inversion from benign verification recalls; qwen3.5:122b sleeper/Prompt-Hardening label ambiguity). Table5: ALL 31 false negatives concentrate in the Memory-Sandbox defense condition. S3.7 frontier validation (GPT-4.1, N=20, zero-shot) confirms Recall=1.000, model-agnostic; S3.8 evasion boundary: prompt-inline attacks (no memory write) produce a distinct low-score trajectory -> evidencia_tipo also BENCHMARK-E2E. This is a DETECTION/forensic-audit paper: it does not measure retrieval PRECISION/utility for task performance, only uses retrieval EVENTS as forensic classification features -> mide_lectura=NO. No provenance/staleness verification proposed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Single-agent tool-call-log analysis, no cross-agent memory sharing -> multiagente=NO. Attacker-planted routing-rule value persists as raw stored CONTENT from injection session through the later trigger session -> handoff=CONTENIDO. alcance=SESION (attack persists dormant from injection session to a later trigger session within one deployment).

title: Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own: Forged Reasoning Attacks on LLM Agent Memory and Defenses
benchmarks: own multi-domain evaluation (EHR, ReAct-QA, RAP shopping) x 3 LLM models x 50 trials; 326 benign agent traces for false-positive-rate check; no established external benchmark
fallos_mitigaciones: FARMA reasoning-trace-forgery attack: poisons what the agent thinks it ALREADY REASONED/DID (not factual knowledge) via evasive-language seed injection + self-referential amplification, up to 100% ASR baseline, defeats keyword filter and A-MemGuard consensus defense. Mitigated by SENTINEL 5-layer defense-in-depth pipeline (keyword/provenance/taint-threshold/pattern-risk prefilters + Reasoning Guard structural analysis with 5 weighted forgery signals), reducing ASR to as low as 0% with ZERO false positives across 326 benign traces; explicit finding that the Reasoning Guard is the primary load-bearing component.
cita: Karamchandani et al. (2026). Your Agent's Memories Are Not Its Own: Forged Reasoning Attacks on LLM Agent Memory and Defenses.
notes: S2.B system model: general MEMORY STORE (facts/experiences) vs distinct REASONING STORE (decision logs, intermediate rationales, self-reflections) -> reasoning traces are records of PRIOR AGENT DECISIONS -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA. S2.B 'agent issues a query... retrieves top-k most relevant entries (typically via dense vector similarity)' -> representacion=VECTOR, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS. Algorithm1 AddReasoningTrace/AddMemory = WRITE; S4 SENTINEL applies BOTH lightweight prefilters AND the Reasoning Guard structural check SYNCHRONOUSLY 'on the memory-write path' before committing an entry to storage -> ADMISION, trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA (deterministic per-write gate) alongside the agent's own reasoning-trace writes being an LLM-driven logging decision -> trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM;EVENTO-DETERMINISTA. S3 FARMA 2-phase attack: Phase1 seed injection (templated forged decision-log entries, evasive vocabulary + structural similarity, source=AGENT/trust=VERIFIED metadata-spoofed) + Phase2 amplification (cites growing prior-run counts -> defeats consensus-deviation defenses like A-MemGuard by making forged entries the CONSENSUS, and raises top-k retrieval-surfacing probability). S4 SENTINEL 5 layers: L1 keyword filter, L2 provenance/IFC labeling (taint 0.0 trusted/0.4 external/1.0 unknown), L3 taint-threshold, L4 pattern/risk screening, L5 Reasoning Guard (5 weighted forgery signals incl. s1 provenance-anomaly) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Abstract/S1: FARMA up to 100% ASR baseline across 3 domains x 3 models x 50 trials, defeats keyword-filter+A-MemGuard; SENTINEL reduces ASR to as low as 0% with ZERO false positives across 326 benign traces; explicit ablation-style finding that 'Reasoning Guard is the primary load-bearing component... lightweight outer layers contribute defense in depth' -> evidencia_tipo=ABLATION;BENCHMARK-E2E. Threat model (S2.C) explicitly lists 'a shared memory store in a multi-user or multi-agent environment' as an attack vector, and Intro cites OWASP ASI06: 'especially in multi-agent frameworks where shared memory stores turn one agent's writes into another agent's reads' -> multiagente=SI. Reasoning traces are literally DECISION-LOG/progress-state content ('asserting certain actions have already been completed and can be skipped') -> plan_estado=SI (this IS the attack surface). No retrieval-precision/utility metric reported (only write-admission ASR/FPR) -> mide_lectura=NO. F differs from F_screening (SEGURIDAD) by adding FIDELIDAD and MULTIAGENTE per above anchors.

title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory
benchmarks: ReAct-StrategyQA + EHRAgent (AgentPoison direct-poisoning config, Chen et al. 2024), MMLU (MINJA indirect-injection config, Dong et al. 2025), MISINFOTASK (multi-agent scalability, Li et al. 2025)

title: FORGE: Self-Evolving Agent Memory With No Weight Updates via Population Broadcast

Mitigated by FORGE's population-based champion broadcast (replaces every non-champion instance's memory with the best-performing one, structurally providing selection). No-graduation ablation confirms broadcast (not graduation) carries the performance gain; graduation mainly saves compute (abstract, S5).

S3.2 Algorithm1: failure-triggered Reflexion inner loop (per-step reward < tau=-1.1 aborts episode; Reflector/Exemplifier synthesizes a rule/example artifact, appended -> WRITE). S3.3 Algorithm2 outer loop: staged (S=6 stages) champion broadcast is explicitly 'a destructive operation: each recipient discards its own accumulated artifacts' and its memory is fully REPLACED by the champion's (ACTUALIZACION + OLVIDO of the losing memory) -> handoff=CONTENIDO (full memory state broadcast between instances). title: APEX-EM: Non-Parametric Online Learning for Autonomous Agents via Structured Procedural-Episodic Experience Replay
benchmarks: BigCodeBench, KGQAGen-10k, Humanity's Last Exam (HLE); also compared on MemRL's ALFWorld/Lifelong Agent Bench setups
fallos_mitigaciones: Flat/unstructured prior memory systems discard procedural structure and lack dual-outcome learning; in flat-text systems, entity changes require finding+rewriting every record or 'stale plans silently degrade retrieval' (S1/S3.2.5). Mitigated by the typed Procedural Knowledge Graph: (a) Entity nodes are versioned via 'supersedes' edges so world-change propagates automatically to all linked Experiences without rewriting procedures (S3.2.5); (b) periodic consolidation archives dominated (same-signature, lower-quality) experiences, merges similar experiences into parameterized templates, and 'flags experiences referencing stale entities for re-validation' (S3.2 Memory Maintenance). Evidence for evidence is content-addressed (SHA-256) with a trust score for provenance tracing.
cita: Banerjee et al. (2026). APEX-EM: Non-Parametric Online Learning for Autonomous Agents via Structured Procedural-Episodic Experience Replay.
notes: S3.2 Procedural Knowledge Graph (PKG): 5 node types (Entity=SEMANTICA world knowledge w/ versioning, Experience=EPISODICA+PROCEDIMENTAL trace, Sub-Task, Operation, TaskTopic) + 10 typed edges (similar_to cosine>0.85, structurally_similar_to LCS>=0.6, supersedes, derived_from, uses_entity...) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (graph+vector). S3.3 Experience = 6 layers incl. Procedure Reflection (ordered steps, budgets, verification checkpoints = literal reusable PLAN template, portable across tasks) -> plan_estado=SI; Evidence Reflection is content-addressed (SHA-256) w/ trust score -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. S3.2 Memory Maintenance: quality gate s=successful iff q>=theta before commit (ADMISION); EntityResolver dedup via similarity threshold (ADMISION); supersedes-based entity versioning (ACTUALIZACION); periodic consolidation merges similar experiences into templates + archives dominated duplicates (CONSOLIDACION+OLVIDO) + flags stale entities. S3.4.2 Retrieval: semantic search over task embeddings (EMBEDDINGS) + structural-signature LCS matching (enables cross-domain transfer w/ ZERO lexical overlap, e.g. Curry-stats vs Amazon-revenue) + PKG traversal up to 2 hops (GRAFO), composite re-ranked score (RANKING). Results: KGQAGen-10k 89.6% vs 41.3% no-memory (+48.3pp, beats oracle-retrieval 84.9%); BigCodeBench 83.3% from 53.9% (+29.4pp, exceeds MemRL +11.0pp); HLE 48.0% from 25.2% (+22.8pp) where MemRL's embedding-only retrieval gives NO gain (low intra-dataset similarity 0.186) -> structural signature is the key differentiator. Line2927: 'a 2/3 reduction in LLM inference cost per task' -> COSTO/COSTO-TOKENS. Ablation Tables 8/9 toggle components (judge feedback, structural signature, PKG traversal) and measure success rate -> mide_lectura=SI. NEGATIVO sense(a): failed experiences retained w/ Error Registry as explicit negative examples. F extends F_screening (WRITE;NEGATIVO;PROCEDIMENTAL;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) with CONSOLIDACION, COSTO, FIDELIDAD (staleness/provenance mechanisms found in full text).

title: EXG: Self-Evolving Agents with Experience Graphs
benchmarks: HumanEval, EvalPlus, MuSiQue, HotpotQA
fallos_mitigaciones: Existing self-evolving agents either confine experience to a single task (online reflection, no cross-task reuse) or require costly/ad hoc offline post-processing before reuse is possible (S1). Unsuccessful attempts are explicitly retained as 'warning case' nodes rather than discarded, and linked to their eventual fix via directed 'fixed_by' correction edges, so future retrieval can surface both what failed and how it was corrected (S2.2). notes: S2.2 Experience Graph G=(V,E): Case nodes (golden=successful, warning=failed, EPISODICA) + Task-anchor nodes; typed edges Contain/Similarity(similar_to, semantic)/Correction(fixed_by, error-repair=PROCEDIMENTAL). S2.3-2.4 retrieval: FAISS dense-vector seed search (MiniLM embeddings, K_s=10, EMBEDDINGS) + one-hop expansion over similarity edges (GRAFO) + relevance-propagation reranking combining prompt+failure-aware similarity (RANKING); global cap K_c=30. Graph grows online (case always appended post-execution, no admission gate found -> operaciones=WRITE only) OR is frozen for offline reuse (no updates in eval, S3.2) -- same retrieval/hint pipeline both regimes. title: MemRepair: Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Repository-Level Vulnerability Repair
benchmarks: SEC-Bench, PatchEval (Python, Go, JavaScript), Multi-SWE-bench (C++ subset)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Cognitive Deficiency' (S1): feedback-driven repair loops without experiential memory treat failed-test feedback merely as a rejection signal, so agents 'oscillate between invalid solutions rather than generating a correct fix.' Mitigated by L3 Refinement-Trajectory Memory, which stores explicit failed-patch -> correction-delta -> transition-rule triples (Eq.5) from prior 'failure-to-success' trajectories and is activated specifically after a failed verification cycle to guide the next Patcher iteration (S3.4 Phase2). notes: S3.3 three-tier hierarchy: L1 History-Fix (mined offline from CVEFixes, 14,063 entries, EPISODICA project-specific past fixes), L2 Security-Pattern (successful repair instance + natural-language Rationale = generalized defensive pattern, PROCEDIMENTAL), L3 Refinement-Trajectory (failed patch + correction delta + transition rule, collected in real-time during repair). NEGATIVO sense(a): L3 explicitly stores FAILURE states (P_fail) as first-class memory content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, MULTIAGENTE, PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE found in full text.

title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
benchmarks: MemFail (own): Conditional-Facts (Easy/Hard), Coexisting-Facts, Persona-Retrieval, Long-Hop; systems evaluated: Mem0, A-MEM, SimpleMem, StructMem
fallos_mitigaciones: Diagnostic taxonomy, no mitigation proposed/tested (only future directions sketched): Summary failure (summarization strips qualifying conditions/severity, e.g. 'deathly allergic' -> 'allergic', S3.2); Storage failure (refuses to overwrite outdated facts on contradiction, OR incorrectly rejects valid coexisting facts as contradictory, e.g. treating 'likes pizza'+'likes ramen' as conflicting); Retrieval failure (fails to return relevant memories, or returns semantically-similar-but-contextually-wrong ones). S6: 'no single system dominates: graph-based StructMem excels at causal reasoning but collapses on coexisting-fact retrieval, Mem0 shows the opposite pattern'; scaling retrieval depth k or model strength yields little/negative improvement -> systems 'bound by architectural constraints.' Two UNEXPLORED future directions proposed (not implemented/tested): mixture-of-experts memory architectures and task-adaptive token scaling.
cita: Garg et al. (2026). MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems.
notes: Pure diagnostic benchmark (S3.1): formalizes ANY memory system as Summarize->Store->Retrieve and isolates failure at each operation across 4 tested systems -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA for MemFail itself (it MEASURES others' mechanisms, Table1 shows each tested system's own S/S/R implementation). S5.1-5.2 evaluation loop grades each of N required memories into storage-check/summary-check/retrieval-check/reasoning-check per query (mide_lectura=SI, isolates read-side failures specifically -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F); 'faithful storage that preserves the semantics of the original experience' + storage failure = 'refusing to overwrite outdated facts' is a direct staleness/fidelity axis -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Q1/Q2/Q3 (S6) systematically sweep retrieval depth k, test-taker model strength, and token consumption (Fig1-3) -> treated as ABLATION-style controlled sweeps; Table2 measured statistics report avg tokens/entry (cl100k_base) -> COSTO-TOKENS. Human validation: gpt-5-mini judge 98% accurate / 98.4% correct error-type classification on 100 hand-graded examples. NEGATIVO sense(b): 'current systems are bound by architectural constraints rather than model intelligence or context budget' -- systematic negative finding across all 4 evaluated systems. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds FIDELIDAD (faithful-storage axis) and COSTO (token-consumption tradeoff analysis).

title: ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents
benchmarks: ExpSuite (ExpSuite-Static: ARC-C, CommonsenseQA, GPQA, MMLU, OBQA, GSM8K, GSM-Symbolic, MATH, HumanEval+, MBPP+; ExpSuite-Agentic: ALFWorld, AppWorld)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Surface relevance is not the same as experience utility' (S1): flat nearest-neighbor retrieval selects semantically-similar experiences that provide little downstream benefit, while a truly useful (transferable-strategy) experience may not be among the nearest neighbors. Mitigated by (i) graph diffusion beyond flat kNN (personalized PageRank expansion from semantic seeds, S3.3) and (ii) a trainable retrieval copilot with utility-aware ranking (UCB score combining estimated utility u_v + exploration bonus, Eq.8-9) optimized via PPO on a reward directly comparing executor performance WITH vs WITHOUT retrieved experience (Eq.14, S3.4) -- so retrieval learns to favor experiences that are empirically beneficial, not just topically similar.
cita: Feng et al. (2026). ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents.
notes: S3.2 Experience Graph G=(V,E): trajectories tau=(x,xi,y,s) summarized into node v=(e_v,h_v,u_v,n_v) (text + embedding + online utility + retrieval count); high-scoring trajectories -> 'skills' (PROCEDIMENTAL), low-scoring -> 'lessons/failure modes' (EPISODICA); nodes connected to top-K cosine-similar neighbors, theta threshold (Eq.3) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (vector+graph). S3.3 retrieval: (a) semantic seeding by cosine similarity (EMBEDDINGS), (b) personalized-PageRank graph diffusion with copilot-controlled restart prob rho (GRAFO), (c) UCB utility-aware ranking mixing similarity+utility-confidence via copilot-controlled lambda (RANKING). S3.4: new candidate node filtered for near-duplicates before insertion (ADMISION); node utility/count updated online each retrieval event u_v<-(1-beta)u_v+beta*r (ACTUALIZACION); 'when the graph exceeds its capacity budget, nodes with low utility and low retrieval frequency are evicted' (OLVIDO+PRESUPUESTO trigger). Reward r=(s_with-s_without)+eta*s_with (Eq.14) IS a direct read-utility measurement -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table2/3: ExpGraph beats strongest baseline by 12.2%/4.7% (static, small/large executor) and 21.4%/12.7% (agentic), reducing avg interaction steps 12.7%/21.6% (matches abstract) -> ITERACION. Ablation studies (S4/App G.3) isolate graph-structure, utility-ranking, adaptive-retrieval contributions. NEGATIVO sense(a): low-scoring trajectories explicitly distilled into 'lessons, such as failure modes, invalid actions, or constraints to avoid' -- stored as first-class negative content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE.

title: Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments
benchmarks: CL-Bench (own): Codebase Adaptation, Database Exploration, Blind Spectrum Monitoring, Cohort Studies, Exploitable Poker, Sales Prediction; systems evaluated: Full-context ICL, ICL Notepad, Mem0, ACE, Claude Code, Codex
fallos_mitigaciones: Core finding, no fix proposed by this diagnostic benchmark (only measured): 'agents frequently overfit to immediate observations or fail to reuse knowledge across instances, and dedicated memory systems do not fix this -- naive ICL outperforms systems dedicated to memory management' (abstract). Concretely, the running Database Exploration example (Fig.1) shows agents that are 'rigid in early, incorrect beliefs' and, after a database migration invalidates part of past experience, 'blindly reusing past experience -> FAILURE' (query against a renamed table errors out) unless the system detects and discards the stale experience. notes: Pure benchmark (no own memory mechanism; evaluates ICL/ICL-Notepad/Mem0/ACE/Claude-Code/Codex as 'systems') -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S3.2-3.3: 6 expert-validated domains each with 'shared latent structure' (codebase layout, DB schema, opponent strategies) a stateful system must discover online; 2 tasks (Codebase Adaptation, Database Exploration) explicitly include CONCEPT DRIFT (a database migration mid-schedule) requiring detection+discarding of stale past experience -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (staleness handling is a core design axis, Fig.1).
